claims.assessment: Tall, imposing, plainspoken, dignified, and skilled at mounted archery.

claims.action: Remonstrated that passing over the legitimate heir would hand the state to outsiders.
Persuaded the emperor to take the imperial grandson on the hunt, preventing Yixin from isolating him.
Drove Yixin, Chun, and their faction from court.
Firmly declined the edict ordering him to marry the Princess of Yue.
Proposed promoting clerks by length of service; the court accepted.
Repeatedly warned that the Jurchen threat was serious and should be met before rebellion.
Retreated into Ningjiang city when Jin forces attacked and Yidiqian died in battle.
Left officials to defend Ningjiang, crossed the Huntong River westward with three hundred horsemen, and the city fell.
Resisted Jin forces with Xiao Dili at Changli Marsh and was dismissed after defeat.
Served as rear guard during Tianzuo's personal campaign and was defeated again.
Defended the Upper Capital against Yelu Zhangnu and forced him to withdraw.

claims.description: Died of illness at age seventy.

claims.assessment: Historians compared his protection of the imperial grandson to Wuzhi's elevation of Muzong.

claims.action: Recommended Xiao Wuna when the emperor asked which clansmen could be employed.
Harmed the crown prince and promoted Chun as heir.
Framed the crown prince and later resented Liu Shen.
Was harmed and falsely implicated by Yixin's faction.
Was protected as the imperial grandson and later succeeded to the throne as Tianzuo.

claims.attribution: Received the emperor's instruction to inform the Prince of Yan about Wuna's loyalty.
Received the emperor's instruction to inform the Prince of Yan about Wuna's loyalty.

claims.action: Cited as a Tang minister whose service did not exceed Wuna's.
Cited for establishing Muzong as a precedent comparable to Wuna.
Falsely accused Wuna of borrowing rhinoceros horn from the imperial stores.
Defected to the Jurchen, after which Wuna warned that they despised the court.

claims.description: Died in battle against Jin forces at Ningjiang Prefecture.

claims.action: Rebelled and attacked the capital but withdrew without gain.
Was a native of Xijin and originally of the Li surname.
Loved learning, had a reputation for poetry, and passed the Xianyong jinshi examination.
Governed Jingzhou well by restraining clerks, checking powerful bullies, and caring for the elderly and poor.
Reviewed backlogged Upper Capital cases and reversed many wrongful convictions.
Cleaned out transport-route abuses, fixed tax quotas, and increased local salaries.
Was sent to Song to mediate peace after Li Qianshun sought help during Song's attack on Xia.
Was summoned to Yuanyang Marsh and consulted on government affairs.

claims.assessment: Was incorruptible and would not take even the smallest gift.

claims.action: Could memorize classical texts after one reading and could read the emperor's mind.
Told his wife not to lose the emperor's favor, strengthening court influence.
Compiled seventy juan of the Veritable Records of the Imperial Dynasty.
Received the final imperial command jointly with Asi.
During Tianqing was allowed to attend court in a small carriage and later treated by the chief physician.

claims.description: Died and received the posthumous title Exalted Father and name Zhongyi.

claims.assessment: Historians praised his talent and diligence but faulted his household conduct.

claims.action: Entered government service during Chongxi.
Fortified the area between the Yazi and Huntong Rivers.
Investigated the crown-prince case alongside Yixin and failed to clear the innocent.

claims.description: Died with the posthumous title Qinhui.

claims.action: Sent envoys requesting peace when Song attacked Xia.
Jointly received the final imperial command with Yelu Yan.
Often entered and left the forbidden precincts and helped secure Yan's favor.
Was from Wanping and bore courtesy name Jishi.
Was quick-witted in youth and later known for literary composition.
Passed the jinshi examination in Chongxi 5.
Urged the emperor to attend to a case report because rulers must value people's lives.
Objected to relocating wealthy households to Chun and Tai Prefectures, and had the order cancelled.

claims.assessment: Was known for legal clarity, mercy, and saving many from wrongful imprisonment.

claims.action: As military commissioner of Chongyi Army, governed quietly; crows and magpies nesting together prompted imperial praise.
As Households Commissioner submitted annual surplus money of three hundred thousand strings.

claims.assessment: Daozong said only Yelu Jue and Liu Shen were loyal and upright.

claims.action: Told the emperor he did not fear Yixin, much less the chancellor.
With Zhao Hui and Han Zao, distributed porridge daily during famine in Yan and Ji, saving countless people.

claims.description: Died in Da'an 2; the emperor was deeply grieved and increased funeral honors.

claims.assessment: Historians praised his thrice serving the Court of Justice, his Households Bureau service, and his loyalty and uprightness.
Was named by Daozong together with Liu Shen as loyal and upright.

claims.attribution: Congratulated Daozong for recognizing worthy men.

claims.action: Helped Liu Shen distribute porridge during the Yan and Ji famine.
Helped Liu Shen distribute porridge during the Yan and Ji famine.
Was from the Hongyi Palace Division and bore courtesy name Susa.

claims.assessment: Was modest, careful, and impartial toward others.

claims.action: Was appointed a sleeping-hall attendant late in Chongxi and rose through important posts for good service.
With Yelu Naye, led two thousand picked horsemen and suppressed Molusi's Northern Zhubu revolt.

claims.description: Retired, received Co-Seal Director rank, and died.

claims.action: Assisted Taizu with merit and became yilijin of the Dielie Division.

claims.attribution: Received assistance from Yiwen during the founding reign.

claims.action: Rebelled as Northern Zhubu chieftain and was suppressed by Hulu and Yelu Naye.
Led two thousand picked horsemen with Hulu to suppress Molusi's revolt.

translationRepairs: Tianzuo, mindful that Wuna was a senior minister of Daozong's reign who had helped settle the succession, often consulted him on policy; Wuna answered without reserve.
Tianzuo, mindful that Wuna was a senior minister of the former reign who had helped settle the succession, often consulted him on policy; Wuna answered without reserve.

s0043 has 先朝重臣, which means a senior minister of the former reign; the Chinese does not name 道宗 here, so 'Daozong's reign' invents a proper name absent from the unit, and 'the former reign' restores the source wording.
